_code_py!A11: * PROVIDER ADAPTER -- the only FRED-specific code. Swap this class for v2.

_readme!A5: A self-contained, reusable template. One workbook pulls credit-risk data from
_readme!A6: FRED (Federal Reserve Economic Data), lands it raw, and presents it as
_readme!A7: formula-driven dashboards plus a geographic stress watchlist for commercial
_readme!A8: loan-portfolio targeting. All code, config and docs live inside this workbook,
_readme!A9: so it can be emailed, opened on another machine, and re-run with one click.
_readme!A12: 1. Install Python 3 (add it to PATH) and the dependencies:
_readme!A13: pip install fredapi xlwings openpyxl pandas
_readme!A14: 2. Get a free FRED API key: https://fredaccount.stlouisfed.org/apikeys
_readme!A15: 3. Provide the key ONE of two ways (never hardcoded in code):
_readme!A16: - set an environment variable  FRED_API_KEY=your_key   (preferred), or
_readme!A17: - paste it into the _config tab: [SETTINGS] -> fred_api_key cell.
_readme!A18: 4. Enable macros when prompted (the button needs them).
_readme!A20: RUN IT  (the workbook is already the finished product; you only add data)
_readme!A21: 1. In Excel press Alt+F8 -> run ExtractFiles. It writes three files next to the
_readme!A22: workbook: runner.py (from the _code_py tab), requirements.txt, and RUN.txt
_readme!A23: (the exact PowerShell commands). Nothing runs inside Excel.
_readme!A25: 3. Open RUN.txt and follow it from PowerShell: install the deps, then run
_readme!A26: runner.py --backend openpyxl against the closed workbook. It pulls FRED per
_readme!A27: _config and writes the data into the file.
_readme!A28: 4. Reopen the workbook -- the formulas recalc into the populated dashboards.
_readme!A29: No key yet? Set _config demo_mode = TRUE before step 1 and use the --demo
_readme!A30: command in RUN.txt (offline synthetic data). For live data, set the
_readme!A31: FRED_API_KEY environment variable or the _config cell. Optional: after
